newsitem.title: GERMANY: CompuServe's German chief leaves firm.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe's German chief leaves firm.

text.p: CompuServe Corp. said Thursday that the head of its German operation, who has been targeted in a crackdown on Internet pornography, was leaving the online service provider to form his own company.
Felix Somm, who was charged in April with distributing banned materials in Germany, was leaving CompuServe to start his own business, the company said in a statement.
Somm was charged with disseminating child pornography, Nazi writings and other materials that are banned in Germany but could be found on parts of the Internet.
Prosecutors are waiting for a court to decide if there is enough evidence for the case to proceed. No date has been set.
Compuserve said previously it would vigorously fight the charges and predicted they eventually would be dropped.
Eva Preuss, general manager of CompuServe GmbH, would run the unit until a successor to Somm is found, the company said.
